Do not score source information omitted from the summary here; that belongs to coverage.

A source-absent abbreviation expansion is not_established even when it seems familiar; briefly explain in the rationale that it is an explanatory expansion, not a demonstrated change to the bill's legal effect. Set error_type to none for supported claims. For contradicted or not_established claims, choose the most specific available category: insertion, substitution, actor, scope, modality, quantity_date, condition_exception, or other. Give a concise rationale. Do not paraphrase quotes or use ellipses. Return only the structured fields.
request.input:
Bill number: HB2256
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 2332
 By Gardenhire

 HOUSE BILL 2256

 By Sparks

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(b)(5)(E), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (E) Notwithstanding subdivision (b)(5)(D), a public charter school authorized by

 the commission, and the local board of education of the LEA in which the public charter

 school is located, may, within thirty (30) calendar days of the public charter school's

 authorization, mutually agree in writing that the local board of education will be the

 authorizer and the LEA for the public charter school, and the local board of education

 shall assume the rights and responsibilities of the charter agreement. The charter

 agreement must be filed with the commission in a manner prescribed by the

 commission. This subdivision (b)(5)(E) does not apply to a public charter school that

 has had its charter agreement renewed on appeal by the commission; and

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-110(b)(1), is amended by

deleting "A charter agreement" and substituting "An initial charter agreement".

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-110(c), is amended by

deleting the subsection and substituting:

 (c)

 (1) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by a local

 board of education, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for

 ten (10) academic years.

 (2) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by the

 commission, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for a term

 of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic

 years, as determined by resolution of the commission.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(g), is amended by

deleting the subsection and substituting:

 (g)

 (1) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by a local

 board of education, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for

 ten (10) academic years.

 (2) If a public charter school renewal application is approved by the

 commission, then the term of the renewed charter agreement must be for a term

 of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic

 years, as determined by resolution of the commission.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(f)(3), is amended by

deleting "Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and § 49-13-

110(c), if" and substituting "If".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(l), is amended by deleting

"Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and § 49-13-110(c), if"

and substituting "If".

 SECTION 7. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change how public charter schools in Tennessee are authorized and how long their renewed charter agreements last. It is a proposal and has not been shown to be law.

First, it would replace Section 49-13-108(b)(5)(E). A charter school authorized by the state charter commission and the local board of education of the school district where it is located could agree in writing, within 30 calendar days of the school's authorization, that the local board will become the authorizer and the school district for that school. The local board would then take on the rights and responsibilities of the charter agreement. The agreement would have to be filed with the commission in the way the commission sets. This option would not apply to a charter school whose charter agreement the commission renewed on appeal.

Second, it would change Section 49-13-110(b)(1) so that it applies to an "initial" charter agreement rather than "a" charter agreement.

Third, it would set renewal terms in both Section 49-13-110(c) and Section 49-13-121(g). If a local board of education approves a renewal application, the renewed charter agreement must last ten academic years. If the commission approves a renewal application, the term must be at least five and no more than ten academic years, set by commission resolution.

Fourth, it would remove opening words from Sections 49-13-121(f)(3) and 49-13-121(l). Those words made the provisions apply notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of 49-13-110(b), and 49-13-110(c). Each provision would now begin simply with "If." The bill does not show what those provisions say otherwise.

The act would take effect when it becomes law.
</summary>
